items.title: 🚀 We pretrained a language model from scratch on an inference-only NPU, with real backpropagation.
items.content_text: 🚀 We pretrained a language model from scratch on an inference-only NPU, with real backpropagation. 🤗 Model: FINAL-Bench/VKORE-46M-NPU 📝 Technical write-up: https://huggingface.co/blog/FINAL-Bench/backpropagation-on-an-inference-only-npu-pretraini "NPUs are inference-only, you can't train on them." We built a counterexample: VKORE-46M-NPU, trained from scratch on a first-gen (2025) inference NPU, 32 chips, no pretrained weights. A 46M decoder-only model (RoPE · SwiGLU · RMSNorm · GQA), char-level, TinyStories. 📏 Why trust it: a falling-loss curve proves nothing. So we trained the same model under identical init, data, and schedule on the NPU and on a GPU reference. · Loss trajectories correlate at 0.99 · Throughput converged to a comparable level The NPU backward pass and optimizer updates do numerically the same work as the GPU, not an approximation that merely trends down. 🧩 One accelerator now covers pretraining · LoRA · inference · quantization. items.title: Crivo-150M is now on the Pareto frontier of the Decision Index 🎯
items.content_text: Crivo-150M is now on the Pareto frontier of the Decision Index 🎯 Scored by the maintainers on the private tests: Full 22.21, the best of all submissions at or below 150M and higher than every model below 0.75B, including models up to 4× its size. Median latency on the board's GPU: 13 ms. It is a 149M typed-decision encoder (Ettin / ModernBERT): a state plus choice, noul or score questions in, a probability for every option out, in one forward pass. Trained on open data only. Next: tasks from new domains, the weak spot of every small encoder on the board. tardellirs/crivo-150m multimodalart/jev-decision-index Thanks to @ multimodalart for the Decision Index and its open kit, @ orionweller and the Ettin team, @ tomaarsen for the Ettin rerankers, @ hotchpotch for the Bekko System One data and @ sileod for tasksource. items.content_text: I’ve just left BananaMind to focus my work on SupraLabs . items.title: Hi everyone, we're back!
items.content_text: Hi everyone, we're back! And we're releasing something major again now, if you have seen Grok Bot, its very powerful, but there isn't really a local alternative yet. Today we're releasing Minds, they're personal AI bots that live on your computer. They can run anywhere, on your phone, on your mac, on windows, and even on linux. They support OpenAI Oauth as the main integration because most people already have a ChatGPT sub. But locally, It supports ANY openai compatible api which allows you to setup ollama and llama.cpp and everything else. It uses Jev for command approval on OpenRouter and Muse Spark Transcribe for transcription. Its fully Open Source! Check it out: https://github.com/BananaMind/Minds See translation

items.title: I added a small gate to the Gated DeltaNet layers of Qwen3.5 and trained it with GRPO under a length penalty.
items.content_text: I added a small gate to the Gated DeltaNet layers of Qwen3.5 and trained it with GRPO under a length penalty. On Qwen3.5-4B it reasons 48% shorter than LoRA on MATH-500, and anytime accuracy goes from 0.786 to 0.852. A LoRA with about the same parameter count barely moves. The gate sits on beta, the per-token write strength. One matrix per layer, zero init, so it starts as a no-op. It started as a negative eigenvalue experiment. The negative range turned out not to matter. The gate did. Write-up: https://huggingface.co/blog/Avifenesh/beta-gate-qwen35 Adapters: Avifenesh/gate-qwen35-6accb63081800b2f2d583b80 Code: https://github.com/avifenesh/gdn-beta-gatehttps://huggingface.co/collections/Avifenesh/gate-qwen35 See translation

items.title: I retracted my own launch claim in public commits, then shipped what
items.content_text: I retracted my own launch claim in public commits, then shipped what survived. MK-SH-1 is a 140M decision model I built on an open encoder. It returns calibrated probabilities, a choice, and an explicit abstention below a frozen gate (tau = 0.79, written down before the curve existed). ECE 0.016 · 90% coverage in-sample; held-out numbers in the card · 106 ms on CPU. Gjusev/MK-SH-1 Demo Gjusev/MK-SH-1-demo Full record, retraction included https://github.com/Gjusev/MK-SH-1 See translation
